author.name: Jarmo Venalainen
author.headline: Studying what AI is, what it can do and what it will do.

comments.text:
The way I see it, the human side of this hasn’t really changed.

People have always entered data into corporate systems in a selective way.

What gets written, when it gets written, how it’s framed, and what gets left out have always been shaped by timing, incentives, attention, and context. AI doesn’t suddenly remove that. It doesn’t make people more complete, more neutral, or more consistent in how they record reality.

So the idea that better outcomes come from people “behaving differently” because AI is present feels off. Most people will continue to enter data the same way they always have.

Where AI does change things is on the inference side.

It can move across domains, connect fragments that were never compared before, and surface patterns that no single person would see in isolation. It can highlight gaps in the data, suggest what should be collected to close them, and expose inconsistencies or anomalies, whether they come from human behavior or from the underlying system itself.

So the shift isn’t in how data is entered.

It’s in how incomplete, biased, and uneven data gets interpreted once it exists.

AI doesn’t fix the inputs.

It makes the structure of those inputs visible.
